svg.title: OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code with PKCE
svg.desc: authorize: The app creates a one-time verifier and sends only its hash. The system browser opens the authorization request. Ada authenticates and approves the requested scope. The server binds a short-lived code to the PKCE challenge. Only the authorization code returns through the app link. exchange code: The app proves it owns the verifier used to start login. The token endpoint hashes the verifier and matches the stored challenge. The consumed code becomes scoped access and refresh tokens. Only the refresh token persists in operating-system secure storage. The short-lived access token authorizes the API request. refresh safely: Later, the access token expires without interrupting Ada. The app reads the refresh token from secure storage. The app presents the refresh token once. Rotation issues a new pair and invalidates the old refresh token. Secure storage atomically replaces the previous refresh token.

g.text: The app creates a one-time verifier and sends only its hash.
The system browser opens the authorization request.
Ada authenticates and approves the requested scope.
The server binds a short-lived code to the PKCE challenge.
Only the authorization code returns through the app link.
The app proves it owns the verifier used to start login.
The token endpoint hashes the verifier and matches the stored challenge.
The consumed code becomes scoped access and refresh tokens.
Only the refresh token persists in operating-system secure storage.
The short-lived access token authorizes the API request.
Later, the access token expires without interrupting Ada.
The app reads the refresh token from secure storage.
The app presents the refresh token once.
Rotation issues a new pair and invalidates the old refresh token.
Secure storage atomically replaces the previous refresh token.
